verdict.rationale: Adyen documents tokenizing shopper credentials and returning ACP/UCP tokens that agents pass to merchants instead of raw card data. The UCP token is bound to a specific checkout session and merchant identifier, which gives merchant and session scoping. Missing for 10: documented amount limits, documented expiry or usage-count controls, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can hand my agent a scoped, limited-use payment credential — amount limits, expiry, merchant restrictions — instead of a raw card number

citations.quote: securely tokenize shopper payment credentials and pass tokens to merchants
Adyen stores the credential and returns an ACP token that your agent passes to the merchant.
Adyen returns a UCP token that is associated with the specific checkout session and merchant identifier.
